# Native manager commands

Use these only after confirming the manager owns the manifest and lockfile. Discovery commands do not apply changes. Show the exact package-to-target map before invoking update commands: for an auto-apply cohort (stable, unpinned PATCH or MINOR targets that pass the resolver checks, see the update policy in SKILL.md) that map is enough, and every target in the ask-per-target set (MAJOR, 0.x, prerelease, exact pin, failed peer/ABI/runtime check) needs the user's explicit approval first. Inspect resulting diffs and run project gates after each cohort.

| Ecosystem | Discover | Apply an approved target |
|---|---|---|
| Go modules | `go list -m -u all` | `go get module@version`, then `go mod tidy` |
| Rust/Cargo | `cargo outdated` | Update the owning `Cargo.toml` dependency/workspace constraint to the approved target if it is outside the current range; then `cargo update -p crate --precise version` |
| Ruby/Bundler | `bundle outdated` | Set the approved target constraint in `Gemfile`, then run `bundle update --conservative gem` |
| Maven | `mvn versions:display-dependency-updates` | `mvn versions:use-dep-version -Dincludes=groupId:artifactId -DdepVersion=version -DforceVersion=true` |
| .NET | `dotnet list package --outdated` | `dotnet add <project> package PackageName --version approved-version` (`<project>` is the project directory or the owning `*.csproj` path) |

For Cargo and Bundler, verify the lockfile resolves exactly to each approved target after the targeted update; if not, stop and report rather than accepting a nearby version. For Gradle, use the repository's configured version catalog/plugin and wrapper; do not substitute Maven commands. Consult `go help list`, `go help get` and `go help mod tidy` for the installed Go version before relying on the Go commands above. Security scanners are ecosystem-specific; run only the one for the ecosystem you confirmed: Go `govulncheck ./...`; Cargo `cargo audit`; Bundler `bundle-audit check` (the tool the README table lists as `bundle audit`); Maven `mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check`; .NET `dotnet list package --vulnerable`; Gradle has no built-in audit task, so use the scanner or plugin the repository configures (for example the OWASP dependency-check Gradle plugin's `./gradlew dependencyCheckAnalyze`, or the repository's own CI task) and report the scanner as unavailable when none is configured; the Node and Python audit commands (`npm audit`, `pnpm audit`, `yarn audit`, `yarn npm audit`, `pip-audit`, and `safety scan` as the README table lists it) are in references/node.md, references/python.md and the README Supported Languages table. Do not use broad upgrade-all commands unless the user has approved their exact target scope and range behavior.
